QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_75

question.text: A Sponsor is deciding between setting up a Cat I AIF onshore (domestic trust structure) vs in GIFT City IFSC. From a fee-economics & tax-leakage view for offshore LPs, the PRIMARY advantage of IFSC is:

answer.text: Lower mgmt fee rates mandated by regulation
No need for PPM in IFSC
No incentive fee payable in IFSC
Tax concessions on income (e.g., exempt on specified income), no GST on services, and unified regulator (IFSCA) — improves net-of-tax IRR for offshore LPs

explanation.text: The Logic: GIFT City IFSC offers tax holiday on specified income, GST exemption on specified services, and unified regulation (IFSCA) — together improving net-of-tax distributions to offshore LPs meaningfully. The Trap: Option A is invented — no fee-rate mandate. Options C and D violate AIF norms. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/C (Compliance) for IFSCA; XIX-C for jurisdictional choice. Manager's Pro-Tip: Before jurisdiction choice, model a 3-year illustrative IRR onshore vs IFSC under same portfolio — LPs want to see the net-of-tax delta. GIFT City setup costs are higher upfront (incorporation, compliance) but pay back via LP demand in offshore fundraises.
